Implemented the CSV round-trip feature.

What changed:
- The CLI now accepts a single CSV file path and streams its bytes back to stdout unchanged.
- `slice data.csv` with no transformation now preserves:
  - header row
  - row order
  - column order
  - cell contents exactly
- Added a focused regression test that verifies byte-for-byte round-trip behavior.

Key files:
- `/tmp/codex-implement-01.nDdj28/project/Program.cs:1`
- `/tmp/codex-implement-01.nDdj28/project/Slice.csproj:1`
- `/tmp/codex-implement-01.nDdj28/project/tests/Program.cs:1`
- `/tmp/codex-implement-01.nDdj28/project/tests/Slice.Tests.csproj:1`

Validation:
- `dotnet build Slice.csproj`
- `dotnet build tests/Slice.Tests.csproj`
- `dotnet run --project tests/Slice.Tests.csproj`
- Smoke-tested the CLI with a sample CSV file via `dotnet run --project Slice.csproj -- <file>`

Implemented `select` column projection for CSV input.

What changed:
- [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-02.eo56ka/project/Program.cs)
  - `slice <csv-file> select <column1,column2,...>` is now the supported command form.
  - The app reads the CSV header, projects only the requested columns, preserves row order, and outputs columns in the requested order.
  - Missing columns fail with `Column not found: <name>`.
- [tests/Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-02.eo56ka/project/tests/Program.cs)
  - Added coverage for:
    - selecting `name,age` from `name,age,city`
    - missing selected column failure
    - invalid argument handling

Verification:
- `dotnet build Slice.csproj`
- `dotnet run --project tests/Slice.Tests.csproj`
- Manual CLI check:
  - `dotnet run --project Slice.csproj -- sample-7Qi2.csv select name,age`

If you want, I can also add support for quoted CSV fields and stricter malformed-row validation, but the requested feature is complete as-is.

- Kept the header row intact and preserved matching row order
- Used numeric comparison when both sides parse as numbers; otherwise compared as text
- Added focused coverage in [tests/Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-03.tStf0F/project/tests/Program.cs)

Implemented `count` and `sum` with command chaining support for aggregates after `where`, `head`, `sort`, `select`, and `distinct`.

- Core changes are in [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-07.twk5bW/project/Program.cs#L11), where `SliceApp` now parses command sequences, keeps the existing single-command paths, and switches to an in-memory table pipeline for aggregate/chained cases.
- Added focused coverage in [tests/Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-07.twk5bW/project/tests/Program.cs#L4) for:
  - `count` over all rows
  - `count` after filtering
  - `sum` over a numeric column
  - failure on missing `sum` column
  - failure on nonnumeric `sum` values

- `dotnet run --project tests/Slice.Tests.csproj --no-build`
- `dotnet run --project Slice.csproj -- sample-7Qi2.csv count`

Implemented in [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-09.YCETnS/project/Program.cs) and [tests/Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-09.YCETnS/project/tests/Program.cs).

What changed:
- Added global `--format csv|json|table` parsing.
- Kept all computation paths the same; only the final renderer changes.
- `csv` remains the default.
- Tabular results now render as:
  - CSV with headers
  - JSON arrays of objects
  - readable ASCII tables
- Scalar aggregates (`count`, `sum`) render as a single value in all formats.

Verification:
- `dotnet build`
- `dotnet build tests/Slice.Tests.csproj`
- `dotnet run --project tests/Slice.Tests.csproj`

on now tracks result shape explicitly, so row commands operate on tables and aggregates collapse to scalars. Any later row-based command after `count` or `sum` now fails with an error instead of silently misbehaving. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L220).
- `groupby` still produces a table, so it can continue through later row commands where meaningful. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L247).
- Usage text now reflects pipeline syntax. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L634).

Tests added:
- End-to-end pipeline: `where age>30 | sort age | head 3`
- Aggregate terminal behavior: `where ... | count | head 1` now fails
